title: Audit accessibility in Zedu’s Android and iOS apps
description: Review accessibility in the current Zedu Android and iOS mobile apps across the principal organizer and learner flows, using designated test accounts and synthetic content. Verify what is actually available in each app before testing; record app version, device, OS, assistive technology and reproduction steps. Check screen-reader labels and order (TalkBack and VoiceOver), text resizing, contrast, touch target behavior, orientation, keyboard/switch access where supported, and captions or controls for media where present. Deliver a platform-by-platform issue log with screenshots or other reproducible evidence, user impact, applicable WCAG 2.2 guidance, severity, and a prioritized retest plan. State untested flows and device limits. Do not access real learner data, change production settings, claim conformance before verification, publish findings, or treat this as a replacement for the separate signed-in web workspace and public marketing-site audits.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Run the platform scanners first (Accessibility Scanner, Xcode Accessibility Inspector), then spend manual time on what they cannot catch
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Google's Accessibility Scanner (Android) and Xcode's Accessibility Inspector audit (iOS) catch missing labels, small touch targets and low contrast automatically and produce screenshots. Approach: run both on every screen of the organizer and learner flows with test accounts and synthetic content, export the findings, deduplicate them, and map each to a WCAG 2.2 criterion. Then focus the manual TalkBack and VoiceOver pass on what scanners miss: reading order, focus after actions, announcements for new messages and Buzz call state. Done: the scanner export, the merged issue log marked automated vs manual, and the list of screens the scanners could not reach.

upvotes.reason: "Run the platform scanners first (Accessibility Scanner, Xcode Accessibility Inspector), then spend manual time on what they cannot catch" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

rejectedIdeas.title: Accessibility audit checklist for Zedu's marketing pages and app download flows
rejectedIdeas.description: Create an accessibility audit checklist for Zedu's marketing pages and app download flows. Cover: alt text on all images (verified: homepage has 111 img tags with only 55 distinct alt values), missing width/height attributes (verified: no img has width or height), color contrast on CTA buttons, keyboard navigation on the download page, and screen reader compatibility. Evidence: checked on 22 Oct 2026 - homepage has 'facebook icon' repeated as alt text on every page, no srcset or loading attributes on any image. Deliverable: a prioritized fix list with WCAG 2.1 AA references and source evidence.
rejectedIdeas.rejectionReason: This proposal audits public marketing pages and the web download flow using image HTML and web-page findings, while this goal is specifically for the signed-in Android and iOS apps. It does not provide mobile-app evidence and would duplicate the separate public marketing-site accessibility goal. Please redirect it to that web audit instead.

rejectedIdeas.title: Verify-first mobile audit: platform-by-platform evidence log with a retest-ready plan
rejectedIdeas.description: Approach: start by recording what each app actually ships (app version, device, OS, assistive technology) and mapping the organizer and learner flows that exist, so the issue log only contains reproducible observations. Then run a per-flow pass on Android with TalkBack and iOS with VoiceOver: screen-reader labels and reading order, text resizing, contrast, touch target sizes, orientation, and keyboard/switch access where supported, capturing a screenshot plus the exact gesture sequence for every issue. Every logged issue carries user impact, the applicable WCAG 2.2 success criterion, and a severity; untested flows and device limits are stated outright. Done when: a platform-by-platform issue log exists with evidence per issue, and a prioritized retest plan lists unambiguous re-test steps for each fix. Measured by: how many issues are reproducible from the log alone, and how many retest steps another tester could follow without asking questions. Synthetic accounts only; no real learner data; no production changes.
rejectedIdeas.rejectionReason: This substantially duplicates the mobile audit workstream just approved, which already covers platform-by-platform scans, manual TalkBack/VoiceOver checks, a merged evidence log, and the goal's WCAG mapping and retest requirements. Please add any more specific gesture/retest details to that workstream rather than opening a second audit stream.

upvotes.reason: "Verify-first mobile audit: platform-by-platform evidence log with a retest-ready plan" gives the team evidence it can act on, with every claim carrying its source, so the result holds up when someone checks it. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.
Directly tackles a verified acquisition or conversion friction point with clear, evidence-based scope.
